claims.text: Tanker sailors continue to face ongoing physical danger while transiting the Strait of Hormuz as of August 2026.
Iran's Supreme National Security Council announced that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the United States changes its military and political conduct.
Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr serves as the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and is a commander in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Iran's demands for reopening the Strait of Hormuz include the lifting of the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, full compensation for war damage, and the unconditional release of frozen assets.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Iran and Oman were close to agreeing on a transit route through the Strait of Hormuz.
An oil tanker owned by Abu Dhabi state-owned energy firm Adnoc was hit by an Iranian missile in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday.
Adnoc stated that more than a dozen of its vessels have been targeted by missile and drone attacks in the Strait of Hormuz since February 2026, resulting in one death and 20 injuries.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported that a vessel east of Khasab, Oman, caught fire after being hit by a projectile.
Approximately one-fifth of global oil and natural gas supplies normally pass through the Strait of Hormuz.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis imposed a blockade on Saudi Arabian ports in the Red Sea starting on July 20.
US Vice President JD Vance told Fox News that Iran informed Washington it has no intentions to charge tolls on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi stated that the Strait of Hormuz will certainly reopen whenever the United States accepts Tehran's conditions.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that maritime traffic had restored to 60 percent of normal levels within two weeks of implementing Clause 5 of the June Memorandum of Understanding.
The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs characterized the missile strike on the Adnoc tanker in the Strait of Hormuz as an act of piracy by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, and the Gulf Cooperation Council issued statements condemning the missile attack on the UAE vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.
A car bomb exploded at a toll plaza on the Pan-American Highway in Cauca, Colombia, injuring two security guards.
The Colombian military attributed the Cauca toll plaza car bombing to two dissident factions of the former FARC guerrilla movement.
Abelardo de la Espriella defeated leftist candidate Ivan Cepeda in Colombia's June run-off presidential election by less than 1 percent of the vote.
Former Colombian President Gustavo Petro pursued a 'Total Peace' strategy beginning in 2022 that emphasized dialogue with armed criminal and rebel groups.
The US State Department pledged $1 billion in security assistance to Colombia following the swearing-in of President Abelardo de la Espriella.
Abelardo de la Espriella broke with tradition by holding his presidential inauguration ceremony in Cali instead of the capital city of Bogota.
President de la Espriella announced that Colombia would join the US-led 'Shield of the Americas' security partnership.
Before entering politics, Abelardo de la Espriella worked as a defence lawyer representing drug-trafficking paramilitary figures.
President Abelardo de la Espriella, who nicknames himself 'The Tiger', vowed during his maiden speech at a military base in Cali to defeat narco-terrorists.
President Abelardo de la Espriella campaigned on promises to reduce the size of the Colombian state by up to 40 percent.
President de la Espriella announced plans to resume aerial spraying of herbicides to eradicate illicit coca crops.
Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche headed the official United States delegation attending the Colombian presidential inauguration.
Outgoing Colombian President Gustavo Petro refused to attend de la Espriella's inauguration and called for mass public protests over unproven allegations of election fraud.
President de la Espriella announced plans to restore diplomatic relations with Israel while cutting formal diplomatic ties with Cuba and Nicaragua.
Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed a trilateral mutual defence agreement during a meeting in Mecca on Friday.
The joint statement from the Mecca agreement stipulates that an armed attack against any one of the three member nations will be considered an attack against all three.
Saudi Arabia and Pakistan previously established a bilateral mutual defence agreement containing a similar collective defence clause in September 2025.
Turkey maintains the second-largest standing military force within the 32-member NATO alliance.
Pakistan Defence Minister Khawaja Asif advocated expanding the Mecca defence agreement into a broader NATO-like military alliance for Islamic nations.
A Turkish official stated that the trilateral Mecca agreement is purely defensive in nature and does not replace existing security commitments.
Turkey provided military support, including uncrewed aerial vehicles and electronic warfare equipment, to Pakistan during India's Operation Sindoor in May 2025.
Pakistan has historically stationed military personnel, fighter aircraft, and air-defence systems inside Saudi Arabia under existing bilateral arrangements.
The announcement of the trilateral Mecca pact coincided with a new military offensive by Yemen's Saudi-backed government against the Houthis.
The US Senate confirmed former Trump defense lawyer Todd Blanche as US Attorney General by a 50-49 vote.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer accused Republicans on X of handing President Trump an excuse to continue widespread corruption by confirming Todd Blanche.
Republican Senators Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski joined all Senate Democrats in voting against Todd Blanche's confirmation.
The US Senate passed a resolution confirming a slate of 71 Trump administration nominees before entering a five-week congressional recess.
Former campaign operative P. Wells Griffith was confirmed as US Ambassador to the International Atomic Energy Agency in Vienna.
Republican Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana provided the deciding 50th vote to confirm Todd Blanche as Attorney General.
During confirmation proceedings, Todd Blanche pledged to abandon a proposed $1.8 billion anti-weaponisation compensation fund.
Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley commended Todd Blanche on X for displaying patience, compassion, and tenacity throughout the nomination process.
Todd Blanche represented Donald Trump as his private defence attorney in criminal proceedings prior to joining the Department of Justice.
Todd Blanche was appointed acting Attorney General in April 2026 after President Trump dismissed former Attorney General Pam Bondi.
Todd Blanche adjusted an agreement granting tax audit immunity to Donald Trump and his sons so that it applies retroactively rather than to future tax filings.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated in Belgrade that Ukraine faces an upcoming winter with virtually no working thermal power plants remaining.
President Zelensky reported that overnight Russian missile strikes and frontline shelling killed 13 people across Ukraine over a 24-hour period.
A three-year-old child was killed and four family members and neighbours were injured during a Russian strike on a village in the Kyiv region.
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic stated during a joint press conference that Serbia has not discussed military cooperation with Ukraine and maintains its policy of not imposing sanctions on Russia.
President Zelensky urged foreign nations to enforce stricter sanctions to prevent international components from reaching Russia's missile manufacturing supply chains.
The Ukrainian Armed Forces launched overnight drone strikes targeting Russia's Ilsky and Syzran oil refineries, causing fires at both facilities.
A drone carrying explosives entered Bulgarian airspace from Romania and detonated near an international gas pipeline without causing injuries.
The Bulgarian Defence Ministry identified the fallen drone as a Maya decoy drone model used by Ukraine.
Ukraine conducts near-daily long-range drone attacks against Russian oil facilities to disrupt fuel supplies used to fund Russia's military operations.
Russian forces launched a renewed overnight barrage of missiles and drones targeting the capital city of Kyiv and surrounding areas early Saturday morning.
US Vice President JD Vance placed a phone call to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, and technology.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended personal congratulations to JD Vance and Usha Vance following the birth of their son.
Prime Minister Modi and US President Donald Trump met in France in June 2026 and instructed officials to negotiate a bilateral trade agreement.
The United States raised overall tariff rates on Indian goods to 50 percent in August 2025 due to India's continued imports of Russian crude oil.
US Vice President JD Vance and Second Lady Usha Vance announced the birth of their fourth child, Alec Neel Vance, making him the first child born to a sitting US Vice President in over 150 years.

The US Senate approved the Lindsey Graham-named bill in an 86-11 vote, authorizing up to 500 percent tariffs on Russian imports and 100 percent tariffs on five key Russian oil buyers, including India and China.
The House of Representatives is not expected to consider the Senate-passed tariff legislation until September following its summer recess.
President Donald Trump issued an executive order in February removing a 25 percent punitive tariff on Indian goods after reaching an interim trade agreement with New Delhi.
Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju and Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi engaged in a public debate on X regarding the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill.
Rahul Gandhi urged Minister Kiren Rijiju to implement the 2023 Women's Reservation Law immediately and without linking it to delimitation.
Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi at his office in the Parliament House complex on Friday, August 7, 2026.
The Shiromani Akali Dal withdrew from the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance coalition in 2020 over disputed central agricultural laws.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay hosted a conference of state MPs to formulate opposition to the Centre's proposed constituency delimitation plan.
Around 21 MPs representing parties including Congress, VCK, CPI, CPI(M), MDMK, and IUML attended Chief Minister Vijay's meeting in Tamil Nadu.
Major regional political parties DMK and AIADMK abstained from attending Chief Minister Vijay's all-party MPs meeting.
Congress MP Karti Chidambaram stated that Tamil Nadu's political representation in Parliament must be preserved at 39 members out of a frozen total strength of 543 seats.
Out of 57 total MPs representing Tamil Nadu across both Houses of Parliament, 37 MPs boycotted the delimitation meeting called by Chief Minister Vijay.
Congress MP Praveen Chakraborty expressed disappointment over DMK and AIADMK boycotting the chief minister's meeting on defend state representation rights.

Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal reversed his party's previous opposition, endorsing the rollout of 33 percent women's reservation alongside a proposed 50 percent expansion of Lok Sabha seats in 2029.
The central government's proposed delimitation agenda seeks to increase the maximum capacity of the Lok Sabha from 550 seats to 850 seats.
